title: Chemistry lab work
titleCn: 化学实验室工作与实验报告

paragraphs.text: Section three. You will hear a lecturer called Dr. Lewis talking to a first-year chemistry student called Layla about her work in laboratory. First, you have some time to look at questions twenty-one to twenty-six.
Now listen carefully and answer questions twenty-one to twenty-six.
Hello, Layla. Now, this is just a general chat about your progress. First of all, how do you think you are getting along with your chemistry lab work?
Well, I'm not sure, Dr. Lewis. I don't feel very confident. I mean, what we do isn't really all that difficult, but I didn't do much science practical work at school.
But presumably, you've been reading the background information for the experiments on the department website. Is that useful?

Well, it depends. The last experiment about freezing points of different liquids, it would have been helpful if there had been more detail on the website about how to actually measure the temperature. We didn't do this as accurately as we needed to, so the information we got wasn't very useful. We were okay with the equipment, but we certainly wouldn't have been if we hadn't read the stuff on the website before. And some of these safety warnings seem a bit extreme too.
But you do have to be aware of the dangers.
Yes, of course.
Now, what about your lab reports? Students sometimes get very behind with these.
The thing is, I don't know where to begin, so I end up putting it off.
Well, try setting aside half an hour just to do a small part of it. Then the rest won't seem as daunting. And it's important to avoid using informal language or language that's too personal.

Yes, I got quite a bit of feedback on that in my last lab report, but the feedback on the introduction was really negative. I like to follow the guidelines. I didn't spend it all describing the experimental method, for example, because that's all given in the lab notes.
Okay.
But apparently, I didn't give enough information about why the experiment was significant.
Yes, you may need to do a bit of work for that. And don't forget to put the correct references in your review of the literature. What was the feedback like for your results and discussion section?

Okay. Apparently, the labeling of the graphs and tables wasn't always clear, but they liked the way I separated out the different effects of temperature and didn't teach on the different possible reaction mechanisms.
Yes, that's good. To link each stage in the experiment to possible explanations rather than treating them separately.
Hmm.
It takes some students a long time to learn how to make those connections.
My summary at the end wasn't too bad either. Though they said I needed more emphasis on how it related to possible future experiments.

Well, it sounds as if you came all right, actually. But you could join what's called the mentor scheme. This is where you talk informally to another student, probably a postgraduate in actual work. Things like how to approach lab reports.

Right. Well, I'm feeling a bit better about things now I've talked to you, but I'm still worried about all the articles and books we're supposed to get through. Would that be something a mentor could help me to learn?
Sure.
That would be really good. And I think the lectures would all make more sense then.
Yes.
So how do I go getting a mentor then? I did see a leaflet about it. Um, I think it said something about the university office.

Oh, they just print the leaflets. I heard leaflets themselves say you need to go through the student services. But actually, I can put you in touch with someone in this department myself. That might be better.
That sounds good, Dr. Lewis. Thanks.
Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions twenty-seven to thirty.
Now listen and answer questions twenty-seven to thirty.
How are you getting on with the reading anyway?
Well, I've been using Chemistry Three quite a lot. It's not too high a level, and I like the way it links the theory and the practice, especially the sections giving real-life examples.
Yes, that's definitely a strong point.
I wanted to read The Chemistry of Water, but it isn't in the library. They said it was out of print.
Yes, that's a pity. It's still one of the best overviews of the topic. Have you ever looked at Introduction to Chemical Bonding?
I got it on order at the library. I was going to buy it, but it seemed a lot to pay for what you get.
Yes, I agree. But I would recommend you read it as soon as possible. By the time you get to the end of the year, it won't be so relevant.
Okay. What do you think about Basic Inorganic Chemistry? Quite a lot of people have bought that. It's not awfully expensive.
Well, it covers a lot, but not in enough depth for this course.
I'd say you'd be better saving your money there.
Okay. Thanks, Dr. Lewis.
Now, the last thing I would
